title: Inserting into a sorted list
prompt: Formulate an inserting function's description and properties. Only the type signature for the insertion function is given. Define any helper functions you require when needed. You get bonus points if you also formulate a generator for better input.
label: Insert

templates.quickcheck:
import Test.QuickCheck
import Reference (insert)

-- Define your helper functions here.


-- Define your properties here
placeholder :: Int -> [Int] -> Bool
placeholder x xs = insert x xs == insert x xs

main :: IO ()
main = do
  -- Add your properties here with quickCheck to be able to run and check them
  quickCheck placeholder
templates.fitspec:
import Test.FitSpec
import Reference (insert)

-- Define your helper functions here.


-- Define your properties in the list properties, 
-- comma-separated and in the form
-- property $ \x xs -> ...,

properties :: (Int -> [Int] -> [Int]) -> [Property]
properties insert =
  [
    property $ \(x :: Int) (xs :: [Int]) -> insert x xs == insert x xs
  ]

main :: IO ()
main =
  mainWith args
    { names = ["insert x xs"]
    , nMutants = 100
    , nTests = 100
    , timeout = 0
    }
    (insert :: Int -> [Int] -> [Int])
    properties

title: Sorting a list
prompt: Formulate a sorting function’s description and properties. Write only the type signature for the sorting function itself; the implementation is provided. Define helper functions as needed. The result should be sorted, have the same length, and contain the same items with the same multiplicities (be a permutation of the original list).
label: Sort

templates.quickcheck:
import Test.QuickCheck
import Reference (sort)

-- Define your helper functions here.


-- Define your properties here
placeholder :: [Int] -> Bool
placeholder xs = sort xs == sort xs

main :: IO ()
main = do
  quickCheck placeholder
templates.fitspec:
import Test.FitSpec
import Reference (sort)

-- Define your helper functions here.


-- Define your properties in the list properties, 
-- comma-separated and in the form
-- property $ \xs -> ...,

properties :: ([Int] -> [Int]) -> [Property]
properties sort =
  [ 
    property $ \(xs :: [Int]) -> sort xs == sort xs
  ]

main :: IO ()
main =
  mainWith args
    { names = ["sort xs"]
    , nMutants = 100
    , nTests = 100
    , timeout = 0
    }
    (sort :: [Int] -> [Int])
